move: slides pixelate to 64px blocks, swap at peak, resolve back sharp
how: A canvas shows three landscape images in equal slots with a slow push-in and drift; the last second of each slot is the transition. Block size rises 1 to 64px on a sine bell shaped by power 1.6 and quantised to steps of 4, drawn by downscaling to a tiny canvas and upscaling with smoothing off, so the image chunks into mosaic and resolves; the next image swaps in at the peak. A title with a small label pops up and fades in on each swap, three dots mark the active slide, and a thin progress bar runs across the full D.
adapt: Replace the three images and names and the label, change slot count (D divides into equal slots), the peak block size 64 and the quantise step 4. Keep the sine bell so pixelation builds and releases symmetrically around the swap.
port: mount(el, shot) creates the canvas, tiny canvas, title, dots and bar and loads images; animate(el, shot, D) returns a timeline with one linear progress tween over D whose onUpdate computes the block size, draws, and updates the UI, replacing fx.register. Wait for image decode before the first frame.
caveats: resizing the tiny canvas every frame is cheap but image-rendering: pixelated must be on the output canvas
images must be reachable from the host
